items.text: Students will read and write 2- and 3-digit numbers (up to 999) using hundreds, tens and ones, write them in expanded form and number names, and count forward and backward by 1s from a given number.

sections.greeting: Draw a table with three columns — Hundreds, Tens, Ones — and write 123 above it.

stories.label: Point & ask
stories.text: Which digit shows hundreds? Which shows tens? Which shows ones? Let a few students answer.

stories.label: Think
stories.text: If I have 1 hundred, 2 tens and 3 ones, how many blocks do I have in all? Today we learn to read and write numbers using hundreds, tens and ones — and say their number names.

sections.title: Hook — build 123 on the place-value table

steps.label: Place
steps.body: In 342, 3 is in the hundreds place, 4 is in the tens place, and 2 is in the ones place.

steps.label: Expanded
steps.body: 342 = 3 hundreds + 4 tens + 2 ones = 300 + 40 + 2. We write 300 because 3 hundreds means 3 × 100.

steps.label: Value
steps.body: The value of 3 is 300, the value of 4 is 40, and the value of 2 is 2 — because of the place they are in.

steps.label: Number names
steps.body: 4 tens is Forty, 5 ones is Five, so we say “Forty-five”. Read 72 as “Seventy-two” — tens numbers (20–90) usually end with “ty”.

cfu.q: What is the value of 4 in 342?
How do we write 45 in words?
6 hundreds, 0 tens and 2 ones = which number?

sections.title: See it in the place-value tables
Practice — solve in notebooks (with answers)
sections.body: Students solve individually, then check together. Walk around; sit beside strugglers and ask leading questions like “Which place is this digit in?” or “What is the tens word here?”
items: Q1: 602 = ___ hundreds, ___ tens, ___ ones  →  6 hundreds, 0 tens, 2 ones
Q3: the digit 6 in 602 is in the ___ place  →  hundreds
Q4: the digit 0 in 602 is in the ___ place  →  tens
Q5: the digit 2 in 602 is in the ___ place  →  ones

sections.title: Conclusion — quick verbal quiz
items: What is the value of 7 in 745?  →  700 (7 is in the hundreds place)
How do we write 83 in words?  →  Eighty-three
